pages.scan: I opened the request JSON and looked at works/auto-6294ee8a2094/workflow/storyboards-unnumbered/page-03.png with Read. It is a storyboard with grey placeholder boxes in five panels: two on the top row, two on the middle row and one wide panel at the bottom. Reading left to right, top to bottom: (1) Top-left panel, caption at the top left: "A later morning: patients can always check in at the front desk." Below it are placeholders labelled "raman" (left) and "meera" (right), with no dialogue, so this is a silent beat between the two of them. (2) Top-right panel, caption at the top: "Some check in ahead on the Welbuk Health app." One placeholder below, labelled "priya", with no dialogue. (3) Middle-left panel, caption at the top left: "Ravi scans the QR code at the door." One placeholder at centre right, labelled "ravi", with no dialogue. (4) Middle-right panel, caption at the top left: "A short form on his own phone, shared with consent." One tall placeholder at the right, labelled "ravi", with no dialogue. (5) Wide bottom panel. First the caption at the top left: "Every check-in gets a slot on the screen." Then the tinted rounded label at the upper right: "A-10 · A-11 · A-12". Below are three placeholders from left to right, labelled "raman", "priya" and "ravi". There is no dialogue; the three of them waiting together is a silent beat.
pages.observation: The reading order is clear: there are no speech balloons, and each panel has one caption at its top left (in panel 2 the caption runs across the top). The page has no nearby out-of-order balloons that could be read in the wrong sequence. All text is legible. "His own phone" in panel 4 clearly points back to Ravi, who is named in the caption of panel 3. In panel 1 the placeholders alone do not show who is the patient and who is at the desk, so the art will have to make that clear. In panel 5, "A-10 · A-11 · A-12" lines up with the three seated people, but nothing says which slot belongs to whom. This is a minor ambiguity, not a reading-order problem. "Some check in ahead" leaves the subject ("some patients") implied, which reads fine after panel 1. In every panel the captions sit above the character placeholders and do not overlap them. I found no blocking issues.
